resolved_findings.title: Fix a strictly positive beta for the constant-order merger consequence
resolved_findings.detail: The exact probability formula is correct, but the last sentence asserts a constant-order merger probability without restricting beta. The linked model permits beta=0, for which the probability is zero; allowing beta to decrease with r also destroys a positive constant lower bound. The cardinality and distance hypotheses alone do not supply it.
resolved_findings.requested_change: State that 0<beta<infinity is fixed independently of r for this consequence, with comparison constants allowed to depend on beta. Keep the exact formula valid for beta=0.
resolved_findings.resolution: Line 7 now permits 0<=beta<infinity for the exact law; line 10 fixes 0<beta<infinity independently of r for the lower bound and allows beta-dependent constants. If the kernel sum is between fixed c1,c2>0, the probability is between 1-exp(-beta*c1)>0 and 1-exp(-beta*c2)<1. The beta=0 case is explicitly zero. No endpoint or parameter-uniformity gap remains.

resolved_findings.title: Specify the derivative convention at lattice-distance cutoffs
resolved_findings.detail: The cutoff kernel (J-r^(-d-alpha))_+ has corners when r crosses a lattice distance. The derivative display currently uses an unqualified ordinary m_p'(r), and the subsequent paragraph invokes C1 integral lemmas. The earlier cutoff and finite-volume notes correctly restrict their derivative calculations to differentiable scales, but that restriction is lost here. In general the cluster moments are continuous and piecewise differentiable, not globally C1 across the activation radii. This is a convention/justification gap, not an error in the stated moment exponents.
resolved_findings.requested_change: Specify right derivatives, or restrict the derivative asymptotic to non-lattice-distance radii/almost every r. Explain that the moments are locally absolutely continuous or continuous and piecewise C1, so the integral arguments of 4E16 and 4E17 apply by integration across the locally finite breakpoints. Do not assert global C1 regularity for these cutoff moments.
resolved_findings.source_comparison: The fixed I v1 defines the cutoff in Definition I.1.5 and uses the closed ball in Lemma I.4.1. Its increasing-r hazard interpretation supports a right-derivative convention; the source's informal derivative notation does not remove the need to state the convention in these self-contained notes.
resolved_findings.resolution: The ordinary derivative is restricted to r outside the explicitly defined, locally finite lattice-distance set D; nonderivative asymptotics remain along all radii. Lines 12-14 now justify continuity by monotone coupling and dominated convergence using finite-cutoff moments, then bound the finite-neighbor derivative formula by C_(p,a,b)*m_(p+1)(b). On a compact scale interval the b-cutoff clusters of the finitely many relevant vertices are finite, and their finitely many candidate incident edges have no activation at a fixed deterministic scale almost surely; this validates the stated stability and domination argument. The polynomial bound has total degree p+1 and is integrable by the cited subcritical moment input. Piecewise continuous bounded derivatives and continuous endpoints give local absolute continuity and finite-piece FTC integration. The reciprocal and logarithmic integrals in 4E16/4E17 therefore apply without assuming global C1 regularity. The new dominated-convergence link targets the actual theorem 0I8I, which was read. All four moment regimes and constants remain unchanged.
